items.title: Spin dynamics and ortho–para conversion in $H_{2}O$ during the phase transition from gas to solid in external magnetic fields
items.summary: The spin dynamics of water ice in the presence of external magnetic fields are investigated. The employedmodel is based on the approach introduced by Buntkowsky et al. (2008), which considers two nearest-neighbor water molecules and yields a four-spin system, as the abundant oxygen isotope has zero nuclear spin.The model is extended to include coupling to external magnetic fields, allowing us to analyze the interplaybetween magnetic dipole–dipole interactions and magnetic field coupling. Two types of configurations areexamined: (i) static, homogeneous fields, corresponding to a time-independent interaction, and (ii) spatiallyvarying sinusoidal fields in relative motion with the molecules, leading to a time-dependent interaction.All computations are performed within the density operator formalism. The ortho/para populations and thetotal spin projections are evaluated during the first tens of milliseconds following the gas-to-solid phasetransition. For static homogeneous fields, we show that increasing field strength suppresses dipolar-induceddepolarization. Assuming that all molecules are initially in the para state, we show that static homogeneousfields can drive the ortho population up to approximately 50%, whereas suitably chosen sinusoidal-fieldconfigurations can increase it beyond 90%. These results are relevant for schemes aiming to preserve ormanipulate nuclear-spin polarization during deposition.
items.author: Chrysovalantis S. Kannis, Ralf Engels, Nicolas Faatz, Simon Pütz et al.

items.title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
items.summary: For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $λ>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant \[ α=\frac{λ(1-2/q)} {12(λt_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\] where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.
items.author: Li Gao, Lijun Wang

items.title: Network nonlocality with tripartite entangled sources
items.summary: Quantum networks are built from independent sources, and their nonlocality has mostly been studied with sources that emit bipartite entangled states. A source of three entangled qubits is richer, since its nonlocality can be tested by the Mermin or the more demanding Svetlichny inequality. We ask how network nonlocality relates to these two single-source notions and find that the answer depends on the wiring. When two central nodes without inputs share every source, Bell-state measurements turn every Svetlichny violation into a network violation, and even all entangled generalised Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states violate the network inequality. When a single central node is shared, the relation reverses, and a network violation requires a Mermin violation of the source. With more sources, the maximal violation depends on whether their number is even or odd, and we give tight bounds for both cases. These results show that the way multipartite sources are wired decides which kind of nonlocality a network inherits.
items.author: Sudip Chakrabarty, Amit Kundu

items.title: Interference-induced dynamical crossovers in quantum walks on disordered square lattices
items.summary: We study discrete-time quantum walks with Fourier, Grover, and Hadamard coin operators on disordered square lattices, alongside classical random walks. Edges in the lattice are absent with a probability, $p$. In this case, both classical and quantum walks exhibit an essentially identical degradation of transport. We then study a general version of this model, in which the existing edges are retained. However, the absent edges are no longer absent, but now become partially transmitting, with a transmission coefficient $f$. We find that the response is now quite sensitive to the walk protocol and coin symmetry. The classical walk exhibits asymptotic stability of the anomalous diffusion exponent, $β(t)$. In comparison, quantum walks exhibit a monotonically decaying $β(t)$ beyond the initial transient regime, leading to the absence of quantum diffusion in two dimensions. We map the transport regimes in the $(f,p)$ plane and identify the contour for $β=1$, which separates the subdiffusive and superdiffusive regimes. We also examine the effective diffusion coefficient, the inverse participation ratio, and the first two moments of edge transmission. We restrict ourselves to analyzing bulk propagation prior to finite-size boundary reflections. The results indicate that quantum transport depends significantly on coin-specific interference and cannot be fully described by transmission statistics alone.
items.author: Ramnarayan Bera, Arijit Roy, Soumyadip Ghosh, Soumen Roy

items.title: Sparse Carleman Embeddings for Nonlinear Discrete Dynamical Systems
items.summary: Discrete nonlinear dynamical systems arise in population models, iterative optimization, and numerical simulations, where computing many iterations can be costly in high dimensions. We study Carleman embedding for forced quadratic discrete systems and its application to quantum state preparation. Under explicit stability and initial-state assumptions, we prove that the truncation error decreases geometrically with the embedding degree, uniformly over all iterations. A central obstacle in discrete time is that the lifted update can become dense even when the original coefficient maps are sparse. We overcome this obstacle by constructing an exact auxiliary linear-system representation that applies the coefficient maps one tensor factor at a time, with row and column sparsities bounded independently of the truncation degree. After rescaling, the associated history system has a condition number that grows linearly with the iteration count, uniformly in the truncation degree. These results yield a quantum algorithm for preparing an approximation to the normalized $n$th iterate with constant success probability. Under coherent input-access assumptions, and for fixed sparsity, stability parameters, and a known positive lower bound on the final-state norm, the oracle query complexity is linear in $n$ and polylogarithmic in the inverse accuracy. Numerical experiments in one and three dimensions illustrate the convergence of the truncated embedding.
items.author: Hsuan-Cheng Wu, Xiantao Li

items.title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
items.summary: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. Th
items.author: M. E. Shirokov

items.title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
items.summary: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.
items.author: Zhi-Yao Ning, Zi-Xiang Li, Naoki Kawashima

items.title: Growth Phase Map of α and \b{eta} Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
items.summary: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of $α$-Ta(110), $α$-Ta(111), and metastable $β$-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) at 300-900 $^\circ$C while varying the O$_2$ partial pressure from a $5.5\times10^{-11}$ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to $2.23\times10^{-4}$ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}\leq4.8\times10^{-6}$ to 19). Without added oxygen, $α$-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O$_2$ pressure of only $2.5\times10^{-9}$ Torr ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}=2.2\times10^{-4}$), $α$-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 $^\circ$C, decreasing to 65% at 900 $^\circ$C. Substantial $β$-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 $^\circ$C and disappearing at 900 $^\circ$C. The apparent $β$(001)/$α$(110) selection energy of $1.07\pm0.16$ eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.
items.author: Marius O. Eji, Tyler J. Kirkpatrick, Ty J. Cawein, Joseph P. Corbett

items.title: Compositional Operational Rank, Smooth Realizability, and Dimensional Reduction
items.summary: Higher-dimensional theories distinguish the dimensionality of a microscopic description from the number of directions accessible to a physical observer. Relating these notions requires not only dimensional reduction, but also a consistent preservation of operational independence across different levels of description. We establish sufficient conditions under which a compositional operational rank is preserved first as the dimension of a smooth integral leaf and then as an observable Fisher-information rank. The key requirement is closure-faithfulness: the smooth realization must preserve the dependency relations of the operational closure, rather than merely its total rank. Together with real representability, constant rank, involutivity, and observer/scale compatibility, this yields a local integral leaf whose dimension equals the operational rank. A further primary-identification condition is required at the measurement level. If an independently specified observer image coincides locally with the primary integral distribution and the admissible protocols provide local resolution, finite labeled-mixture closure, and locally constant outcome support, then the same rank can be realized by a finite composite Fisher-information protocol. The construction holds for arbitrary finite rank. At r = 4 it provides a conditional operational criterion for dimensional reduction in higher-dimensional theories: a viable reduction must preserve the relevant operational dependency structure, not merely produce four effective coordinates. Quantum-hardware negative controls further show that the same restricted Fisher rank can conceal different larger ranks under a broader pre-specified measurement protocol. The framework therefore constrains the operational outcome of dimensional reduct
items.author: Nikolay D. Tulupov, Alexander M. Tishin

items.title: Competing coherence geometries in positive maps: positivity hierarchies, atomicity, and optimal entanglement witnesses
items.summary: We introduce a family of positive maps on qudits whose Choi operators combine two competing coherence patterns: independent exchange couplings and a collective set of diagonal couplings. For every mixed member of the family, we derive exact conditions for positivity, complete positivity, and all intermediate levels of k-positivity, and we determine the complete phase structure of decomposability and atomicity. The higher-positivity thresholds depend on the channel multiplicities, whereas the exact decomposability boundary is universal in scale-free coordinates. Its proof combines an explicit positive-plus-copositive decomposition with a matching family of positive-partial-transpose (PPT) states. The latter form PPT edge states whose detection region is an ellipse, or a disk after collective rescaling. An embedded-qutrit certificate shows that indecomposability and atomicity coincide throughout the mixed family. In contrast, the purely collective endpoint is decomposable over its entire positive interval. Finally, at maximal coherence, an explicit positive subtraction produces an atomic optimal entanglement witness with the spanning property and a strictly larger PPT- detection set. The study thus provides an exactly solvable setting in which k-positivity, decomposability, atomicity, PPT-edge-state geometry, and witness optimality can be compared in arbitrary local dimension.
items.author: Massimiliano F. Sacchi

items.title: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
items.summary: Real-time decoding is a fundamental necessity for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. In this work, we introduce decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification (DAWG), an ensemble based approach that combines Tanner graph sparsification with ensembling belief-propagation (BP) decoders. The DAWG decoder runs BP decoders over the full detector error model Tanner graph for certain iterations to then transfer the posteriors to a sparsified graph in which additional rounds of BP are run. Each of the decoders in the ensemble uses a different transfer matrix to map the posterior information to the sparsified graph. We use the serial schedule for the minimum-sum BP decoders and, thus, employ Vibe decoding ideas by randomizing the schedules of each of them. The performance of the DAWG decoder is then numerically studied for bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color code circuits to be compared with other state-of-the-art decoding approaches. Importantly, the DAWG decoder shows a similar performance to Relay belief-propagation and Vibe decoding when combined with an order-$0$ Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-$0$) post-processor. Crucially, the post-processor is called an order of magnitude less times than for Vibe with the same ensemble size, indicating that the introduced latency tail will be minimal. Furthermore, LSD-$0$ operates on a sparsified decoding graph of a fraction of the size of the full detector error model, which simplifies the resources required by specialized hardware to support it. Overall, the DAWG+LSD-$0$ decoder represents a viable low-cost BP-based decoding algorithm for quantum error correction codes.
items.author: Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Francisco Garcia-Herrero, Ruben M. Otxoa, Reza Dastbasteh

items.title: Parametrically Enhanced Ergotropy and Charging Power in a Three-Mode Bosonic Quantum Battery
items.summary: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.
items.author: Mustapha Tarboun, Mohamed Amazioug

items.title: Distillable entanglement is continuous
items.summary: We prove continuity of distillable entanglement, the optimal asymptotic rate at which copies of a bipartite state can be converted into maximally entangled pairs by local operations and classical communication (LOCC) with vanishing error. We establish an explicit asymptotic continuity bound that holds for arbitrary bipartite states and depends logarithmically on the system dimension. This bound has the same structure as known continuity bounds for conditional entropy, entanglement cost, and relative entropy of entanglement. Our proof constructs an explicit LOCC protocol that converts either of two arbitrary bipartite states into the other at an ebit cost that vanishes as their trace distance tends to zero.
items.author: Lukas Schmitt, David Sutter

items.title: Nonlinear coupling between motional modes in trapped-ion quantum processors
items.summary: Trapped-ion crystals are a leading platform for quantum information science, but achieving the high-fidelity entangling gates required for fault-tolerant quantum computing becomes harder as system size increases. As systems scale, spectral crowding makes low-order nonlinear resonances between collective motional modes increasingly common and can limit gate performance, especially in monolithic or global-mode architectures. We develop a general model to identify and simulate nonlinear motional-mode coupling (NoMoCou) arising from third-order Coulomb terms and quantify its impact on the Molmer-Sorensen gate across linear chains and 2D crystals in rf and Penning traps. We delineate the regimes where NoMoCou dominates the error budget and provide design rules: detune operating points from low-order resonances, tune trap anisotropy to reshape spectra, and shape gate waveforms.
items.author: Wes Johnson, Brandon Ruzic

items.title: Early-time dynamics of heavy-ion collisions through energy correlators: Celestial blocks and the spacetime structure of out-of-equilibrium QCD matter
items.summary: Ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions provide a unique window into far-from-equilibrium states of QCD matter. The initial stages of these events are characterized by highly anisotropic, nonthermal dynamics that precede hydrodynamization, yet they remain largely inaccessible through conventional soft observables. In this work, we show that the substructure of mid-rapidity jets provides direct sensitivity to the spacetime structure of this early, anisotropic phase. Using classical Yang-Mills simulations and effective kinetic theory to model the early-time evolution of the jet quenching parameter, we compute the azimuthally differential energy-energy correlator within the BDMPS-Z framework. By decomposing the result into celestial blocks, we isolate the coefficients that encode the anisotropic geometry and dynamics of the underlying medium. We identify an observable that couples directly to spatial anisotropies in the out-of-equilibrium QCD matter and also discuss the impact of medium response on its behavior. We further extend our study to mid-rapidity jets generated with the JEWEL Monte-Carlo, adjusted to incorporate an anisotropic medium background, and find qualitative agreement with the analytical expectations. Finally, we discuss how higher-point energy correlators and generalized energy-flow operators can enhance the sensitivity to the microscopic structure of far-from-equilibrium QCD matter.
items.author: João Barata, José Guilherme Milhano, Andrey V. Sadofyev, João M. Silva

items.title: Bell and EPR experiments with signalling data
items.summary: Abstract The no-signalling principle is a fundamental assumption in Bell-inequality and quantum-steering experiments. Nonetheless, experimental imperfections can lead to apparent violations beyond those expected from finite-sample statistics. Here, we propose extensions of local hidden variable and local hidden state theories that allow for bounded, operationally quantifiable, amounts of signalling. We show how non-classicality tests can be developed for these models, both through exact methods based on the full set of observed statistics and through corrections to the standard Bell and steering inequalities. We demonstrate the applicability of these methods via two scenarios that feature apparent signalling: an IBM quantum processor and post-selected data from inefficient detectors.
items.author: Lucas Maquedano, Sophie Egelhaaf, Amro Abou-Hachem, Jef Pauwels et al.

items.title: Classical simulability from operator entanglement scaling
items.summary: Local-operator entanglement (LOE) quantifies the nonlocal structure of Heisenberg operators and serves as a diagnostic of many-body chaos. We provide rigorous bounds showing when an operator can be well-approximated by a matrix-product operator (MPO), given asymptotic scaling of its LOE $α$-Rényi entropies. Specifically, we prove that a volume law scaling for $α\geq 1$ implies that the operator cannot be approximated efficiently as an MPO while faithfully reproducing all expectation values. On the other hand, if we restrict to correlations over a relevant sub-class of (ensembles of) states, then logarithmic scaling of the $α< 1$ entropies implies MPO simulability. This result covers a range of relevant quantities, including infinite temperature autocorrelation functions, out-of-time-ordered correlators, and average-case expectation values over ensembles of computational basis states. Beyond this regime, we provide numerical evidence together with a random matrix model to argue that this simulability result also typically holds for arbitrary states. Our results put on firm footing the heuristic expectation that a low operator entanglement implies efficient tensor network representability, extending celebrated foundational results from the theory of matrix-product states and providing a formal link between quantum chaos and classical simulability.
items.author: Neil Dowling

items.title: Quantum protocols for time synchronisation and distribution: a critical assessment
items.summary: Precise time synchronisation underpins critical infrastructure from telecommunications and financial markets to power grids and scientific metrology. Several families of quantum protocols have been proposed and demonstrated for clock synchronisation and time distribution, exploiting entangled photon pairs, quantum key distribution (QKD) correlations, Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, and entangled clock networks. We critically assess these approaches, reviewing the main quantum time synchronisation (QTS) protocol families, quantifying the gap between theory and experiment, and identifying practical bottlenecks in sources, detectors, and channels. We survey the classical timing landscape from Network Time Protocol (NTP) and GPS to laboratory-grade optical frequency transfer, and compare quantum and classical methods at equivalent maturity. We examine use cases including financial trading, power grids, telecommunications, scientific metrology, and military applications, evaluating whether quantum timing offers a realistic advantage. We show that time transfer, not clock performance, is now the bottleneck for distributed optical timekeeping: the best demonstrated quantum synchronisation uncertainty (2.46 ps, over 20 km of fibre) falls two to three orders of magnitude short of what optical clocks with fractional frequency uncertainties of 10 −18 –10 −19 require. The best deployed link, ELSTAB, calibrates to a few tens of picoseconds in the laboratory and to about 0.2 ns on its 421 km field installation, a further factor of twenty to a hundred behind, while research-grade classical links using optical frequency combs already reach the regime the clocks require, though none is in operational service. items.title: Zak-OTFS: A Predictable Physical Layer for Communications and Sensing
items.summary: This tutorial derives the mathematical foundations of what it means for a carrier waveform to be predictable and non-selective. We focus on Zak-OTFS, where each carrier waveform is a pulse in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, formally a quasi-periodic localized function with specific periods along delay and Doppler. Viewed in the time domain, the Zak-OTFS carrier is realized as a pulse train modulated by a tone (termed a pulsone). We start by providing physical intuition, describing what it means for the Zak-OTFS carrier waveforms to be geometric modes of the Heisenberg-Weyl (HW) group of discrete delay and Doppler shifts that define the discrete-time communication model. In fact, we show that these geometric modes are common eigenvectors of a maximal commutative subgroup of our discrete HW group. When the channel delay spread is less than the delay period, and the channel Doppler spread is less than the Doppler period, we show that the Zak-OTFS input-output (I/O) relation is predictable and non-selective. Given the I/O response at one DD point in a frame, it is possible to predict the I/O response at all other points, without recourse to some mathematical model of the channel. While it may be intuitive that geometric modes of the HW group are predictable and non-selective wireless carriers, this is not a requirement. We provide a necessary and sufficient condition that depends on the ambiguity properties of the basis of carrier waveforms. In fact, we show that the structure of a pulse train modulated by a Hadamard matrix is common to several families of waveforms proposed for 6G, including Zak-OTFS, AFDM, OTSM and ODDM.
items.author: Sandesh Rao Mattu, Nishant Mehrotra, Venkatesh Khammammetti, Robert Calderbank

items.title: Noise spectroscopy of insulating and itinerant altermagnets
items.summary: One of the central goals in the emergent field of altermagnetism is the unambiguous experimental identification and characterization of altermagnetic order across a variety of compounds. This motivates exploring tools that can clearly distinguish altermagnets from antiferromagnets, based on symmetry signatures, and offer access to the dominant orbital character (e.g., $d$-wave vs. $g$-wave) of the magnetic order parameter. In this work, we theoretically explore the potential of noise magnetometry for this task, studying contributions from both magnons and itinerant electrons in different regimes and scenarios. While altermagnetism and antiferromagnetism also lead to different noise spectra for magnons, we find the most striking and symmetry-sensitive signatures in the charge fluctuations of itinerant altermagnets. Both for the homogeneous bulk case and in the presence of strain and/or around domain walls, we identify noise contributions that are only permitted by symmetry in the altermagnet and, thus, provide a unique signature of altermagnetism. Furthermore, the angular dependence of noise around domain walls also offers access to the orbital character of the altermagnet. On a more technical note, we discuss the role and relevance of lattice effects related to the dipole tensor. We hope that our work will help pave the way towards the clear experimental identification of altermagnetism across a wide range of candidate materials.
items.author: Lucas V. Pupim, Mathias S. Scheurer

items.title: Cosmo-SPINN: Fuzzy Dark Matter Simulations with Physics-informed Generative Networks
items.summary: Abstract Generative machine learning models have recently emerged as powerful tools for producing cosmological simulations. However, many existing emulators do not explicitly enforce the underlying physical dynamics governing cosmological evolution, often leading to artifacts and poor adherence to the evolution equations. In this work, we present a physics-informed generative U-Net framework for fuzzy dark matter (FDM) that addresses two complementary tasks: (i) the evolution of cosmological fields from initial conditions across a specified range of cosmological scale factors, and (ii) the super-resolution of FDM simulations at a specified cosmological scale factor. Our model incorporates a physics-informed loss function that explicitly enforces consistency with the underlying Schrödinger–Poisson (SP) dynamics during training. For the evolution task, we find that the inclusion of this physics-based loss significantly improves the quality of the predicted simulations, even when only a small amount of training data is available. Using 20% of the snapshots randomly sampled across the evolution interval, the model accurately interpolates the evolution between the sampled training snapshots in a 1 h −1 Mpc box. Furthermore, the framework generalizes effectively across previously unseen realizations of the initial conditions. For the super-resolution task, we present, for the first time, a generative super-resolution model trained on FDM simulations obtained by solving the full SP equations, considering both single and multiple realizations of the initial conditions and analyzing the role of the physics-informed loss in each case. Our approach enables modern generative modeling of cosmological simulations while maintaining physical consistency and substantially reducing gener

items.title: The imaginary component of the weak momentum: Spectral vanishing and gauge invariance
items.summary: Abstract We establish a rigorous functional-analytic framework for the imaginary component p I of the complex weak momentum p Q = p R + ip I , defined as the imaginary part of the local momentum field ℏ i ∇ ln ψ. For all wavefunctions in the Sobolev space H 1 (Ω), including those with nodal sets, we prove that the expectation value of p I vanishes identically -a structural consequence of the regularity of the probability density ρ = |ψ| 2 rather than a dynamical coincidence -so that the imaginary component carries no contribution to the physical momentum expectation value. The derivation makes no appeal to the polar form ψ = Re iS/ℏ and holds for any ψ ∈ H 1 (Ω). We further prove four structural results: (i) the quantum potential of Bohm arises entirely from p I , and its expectation value satisfies the exact identity ⟨V qu ⟩ = ⟨p 2 I ⟩/2m, proved via Sobolev integration by parts without invoking the polar form -from which the known Fisher information relation ⟨V qu ⟩ = ℏ 2 I[ρ]/8m [1, 2] follows as a corollary; (ii) the group velocity of a Bloch band is the density-weighted average of the local transport velocity p R /m with no contribution from p I ; (iii) the decomposition is gauge-invariant under magnetic minimal coupling, with the vector potential acting exclusively on the real component p R ; and (iv) the result extends to curved Riemannian manifolds, establishing the decomposition as an intrinsic property of the wavefunction independent of any particular representation. Together, these results provide a rigorous operator-theoretic framework for the imaginary weak momentum, while preserving the spectral integrity of linear quantum theory.

This book asks how much of physical structure is fixed by those demands. Recognition Science begins with the distinctions already exhibited by actual operations and follows their consequences. Its central arguments remove alternatives: a conserved comparison selects a quadratic reading; its residual and reference fix a normalized cost; preservation of additive comparisons, together with a first costly join, fixes golden scaling. A retained linking observation selects three spatial dimensions under its stated realization conditions. Further constructions ask how the resulting source evolves, transfers energy and leaves records. The argument is technical because the alternatives matter. A theorem that selects one cost from a specified class says exactly which other costs fail and why. Changing the class can change the conclusion. items.title: Flat Chern bands and correlated states in spiral magnet
items.summary: Flat topological bands provide a promising platform for realizing exotic correlated quantum phases such as fractional Chern insulators. Here, we predict the van der Waals monolayer ReAg 2 Cl 6 hosts isolated flat Chern bands at the Fermi level in its 120 ∘ antiferromagnetic ground state. Their flatness and nontrivial topology arise from the interplay between coplanar spin order and strong spin-orbit coupling within Re 5 d orbitals, providing a mechanism distinct from moiré systems. The spiral spin texture naturally enlarges the unit cell, reducing carrier densities while preserving sizable interaction scales. Many-body calculations show that fractional fillings of the flat bands can stabilize correlated phases, including fractional Chern insulators and charge-density-wave states. Moreover, the mechanism is generic to a broad family of Re-based compounds, with both spin configuration and flat band topology electrically tunable. These findings establish Re-based coplanar antiferromagnets as a robust, tunable, and experimentally accessible platform for flat Chern bands and correlated topological phases potentially at elevated temperatures.

items.title: Spin-adapted neural network wavefunctions in real space
items.summary: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the Spin-Adapted Antisymmetrization Method (SAAM), a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. In the context of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo (NNQMC), SAAM leverages the expressiveness of deep neural networks to capture electron correlation while enforcing exact spin adaptation via group representation theory. This framework provides a principled route to embed physical priors into otherwise black-box neural network wavefunctions, yielding a compact representation of correlated system with neural network orbitals. Compared with existing treatments of spin in NNQMC, SAAM is more accurate and efficient, achieving exact spin purity without any additional tunable hyperparameters. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we apply SAAM to study the spin ladder of iron-sulfur clusters, a long-standing challenge for many-body methods due to their dense spectrum of nearly degenerate spin states. Our results reveal accurate resolution of low-lying spin states and spin gaps in [Fe$_2$S$_2$] and [Fe$_4$S$_4$] clusters, offering new insights into their electronic structures. In sum, these findings establish SAAM as a robust, hyperparameter-free standard for spin-adapted NNQMC, particularly for strongly correlated systems.

items.title: Photonic Neuromorphic Processing With Coupled Spiking Silicon Microrings
items.summary: ABSTRACT Understanding the physical computing mechanisms of individual network nodes is essential for scaling neuromorphic photonic architectures. This work proposes a compact passive nonlinear photonic core based on a side‐coupled integrated spaced sequence of resonators (SCISSOR) comprising three nominally equal microrings and investigate its computing capabilities. Its nonlinearities and internal feedback enable analogue, spiking, and bistable responses that are accessed by tuning the injection power and wavelength. Implemented as a single nonlinear node in a time‐multiplexed reservoir computing, the SCISSOR achieves error‐free classification on the Iris dataset and accuracies above 97 on the Sonar task, using both analogue and digital reservoir representations with 150 virtual nodes. In the digital scheme, spiking dynamics naturally generate sparse reservoir states, enabling efficient classification even with a single spike. Intriguingly, operating points at the boundaries where sharp transitions in dynamical complexity and/or output power occur support high task‐performance, opening novel strategies for future on‐chip training. Spiking and thermal bistabilities also participate to enhance the computational performance. These results suggest that coupled optical microrings can serve as compact, physically interpretable nonlinear building blocks for future neuromorphic photonic processors, particularly in optical‐domain preprocessing and sensing scenarios where kHz‐to‐MHz signal bandwidths are relevant.

items.summary: Abstract Magnesium ions play an essential role in many biological processes but remain challenging to model in biomolecular simulations. items.title: Neuro‐Driven Mechanically Programmable Metasurface for Electromagnetic Environment‐Illusion Generation
items.summary: ABSTRACT Invisibility cloaks are evolving beyond passive scattering suppression toward the active control of radar perception. However, on‐demand generation of electromagnetic environment illusions remains challenging. Passive metasurfaces are fixed after fabrication, whereas electrically reconfigurable metasurfaces usually require dense bias networks and continuous electrical holding power, which complicate large‐aperture integration and introduce steady‐state energy consumption. Here, we report an X‐band neuro‐driven mechanically programmable metasurface (NMPM) that generates prescribed electromagnetic signatures through mechanically retained coding states. To map target scattering profiles onto implementable mechanical configurations, we develop a calibration‐assisted, physics‐guided neural programming framework. This framework compensates for coupling‐induced model mismatch and addresses the non‐unique inverse mapping from desired electromagnetic responses to discrete array states. The generated states are physically written by rotating reflective meta‐atoms optimized for linearly polarized illumination, allowing the programmed configuration to be retained without continuous electrical bias. Microwave experiments on two representative target environments demonstrate that the NMPM reproduces the dominant main‐lobe directions and overall sidelobe envelopes of the target scattering profiles. Quantitative measurements yield cosine similarities of 94%–98%, with consistent agreement under the tested incidence‐angle and frequency variations. These results demonstrate a mechanically retained and algorithmically calibrated route toward adaptive radar deception, electromagnetic scene engineering, and reconfigurable sensing architectures.

items.title: Weak Measurement for Characterizing Effective Jones Matrices of Phase Gradient Metasurfaces
items.summary: ABSTRACT Pancharatnam‐Berry phase gradients generated by spatially rotated meta atoms are widely used to control optical wavefronts with metasurfaces. Here, we develop a weak measurement method for characterizing the effective Jones matrix parameters of fabricated PB phase gradient metasurfaces. In the specified effective Jones model, the local polarization response is described by the amplitude ratio and phase difference, while the spatial rotation of the meta atoms determines the PB phase gradient. By scanning the imaginary part angle and real part angle, the spin dependent deflection is converted into a two dimensional centroid map. The amplitude ratio, phase difference, and phase gradient produce different spatial features in this map, providing information for their distinction and retrieval. For a fabricated metasurface with a known phase gradient, the amplitude ratio and phase difference are obtained by fitting the measured centroid response with the theoretical model. When all three parameters are unknown, three independently trained machine learning models retrieve the amplitude ratio, phase difference, and phase gradient from the same complete centroid map and its angular coordinates. These results establish two dimensional weak measurement as an optical approach for characterizing the effective parameters of PB phase gradient metasurfaces.

items.title: Wolf-pack intelligence with multi-leadership Wolf search hybrid model for text-based deception-risk assessment in executive background checks
items.summary: Text-based deception-risk assessment in executive background checks is a challenging task because potentially misleading statements must be identified from linguistically complex and highly imbalanced data. This paper proposes a Multi-Leadership Wolf Search Algorithm (ML-WSA)-based framework for automated deception-risk assessment and statement prioritization. The core contribution lies in a dynamic multi-leadership search mechanism that enables parallel exploration of multiple regions in high-dimensional feature space, effectively alleviating premature convergence in traditional Grey Wolf Optimization. ML-WSA integrates a nonlinear convergence strategy and Cauchy mutation to balance global exploration and local exploitation. To capture deceptive linguistic cues, a dual-channel feature representation combining BERT-based semantic embeddings and linguistic statistical features is constructed, and a semantic-constrained oversampling method is introduced to address minority-class scarcity. Experimental results show that the complete ML-WSA-based framework achieves an F1 score of 0.8733 (95% CI: 0.861–0.886) and an AUC of 0.9012, significantly outperforming standard GWO and BERT fine-tuning baselines (adjusted p < 0.001). Cross-dataset evaluations on three heterogeneous public deception benchmarks provide evidence of robustness under domain shift, with a macro-average F1 of 0.8067. These results support the potential of the integrated framework for human-supervised text-based deception-risk screening under high-stakes conditions.

items.summary: Sound propagation in seas can be effectively predicted so that procedures like communication between submarines, sonar identification, and preservation of marine ecosystems can be established. The current paper will build upon a state of the art framework in boundary element method (BEM) towards the modeling of low/mid-frequency acoustic wave propagation in complex aquatic structures with variable bathymetry, stratified sediment and variable thermoclines. It employs the underwater acoustics modeling of infinite domain by using Greenfunction formulations and non-reflecting conditions used to deal with the modeling boundaries. A hybrid parallelization member of MPI and open MP is used to enable the scalability of its computing capabilities to HPC clusters. When compared to experimental measures of hydrophones arrays in shallow water test sites it is found that the model captures multipath interference and swings in intensity better than current semi-empirical models. items.title: In Situ Electric Tuning―An Emerging STM Tactic for Probing Exotic Quantum Materials
items.summary: ABSTRACT In situ electric tuning (ISET) integrated with scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM/STS) has established itself as a highly effective methodology for controlling quantum electronic states in low‐dimensional materials. This approach combines the sub‐atomic spatial resolution and meV‐resolved spectroscopic capability of STM with the reversible and continuously tunable carrier modulation of field‐effect device architectures. To date, this approach has been applied to numerous systems, including graphene‐based van der Waals heterostructures, correlated electron systems, and moiré superlattice systems hosting emergent quantum phases. Herein, we systematically summarize the state‐of‐the‐art experimental implementations, including global electrostatic gating, tip‐induced local gating, tip‐induced voltage pulse, and in‐plane electric tuning, accompanied with distinct physics under each configuration. We then highlight key representative advances in resolving gate‐dependent band renormalization, correlated insulating states, charge ordering, symmetry breaking, and electrically driven metastable phases at the nanoscale. We discuss practical limitations, such as restricted carrier‐density ranges, tip‐induced perturbations, dielectric reliability, and challenges in decoupling electric effects from current injection and Joule heating. Looking forward, we outline future directions in device engineering, including programmable local electrostatics, scalable architectures, and integrated platforms for operando studies, highlighting their potential to enable deterministic control of emergent quantum phases in functional materials.

items.title: Hook Immanantal Inequalities for Totally Nonnegative Matrices
items.summary: Given a weakly decreasing positive integer sequence $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\dotsc,\lambda_\ell)$ summing to $n$, let $\chi^\lambda$ denote the irreducible character of the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$ indexed by $\lambda$. This representation has dimension $\chi^\lambda(e)$, where $e$ is the identity element of $\mathfrak{S}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^\lambda}$ denote the corresponding irreducible character immanant, the function on $n \times n$ matrices $A = (a_{i,j})$ defined by$$\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^\lambda}(A) := \negthickspace \sum_{w \in \mathfrak{S}_n} \negthickspace \chi^\lambda(w) \hspace{.5mm} a_{1,w_1} \cdots a_{n,w_n}.$$Merris conjectured [Linear Multilinear Algebra 14 (1983) pp. 21--35] and Heyfron proved [Linear Multilinear Algebra 24 (1988) pp. 65--78] that irreducible character immanants indexed by "hook" sequences $(k, 1, \dotsc, 1)$ satisfy the inequalities$$\frac{\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^n}(A)}{\chi^{n}(e)}\geq \frac{\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^{n-1,1}}(A)}{\chi^{n-1,1}(e)}\geq \frac{\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^{ n-2,1,1}}(A)}{\chi^{n-2,1,1}(e)}\geq \cdots \geq \frac{\mathrm{Imm}_{\chi^{1,\dotsc,1}}(A)}{\chi^{1,\dotsc,1}(e)},$$whenever $A$ is an $n \times n$ Hermitian positive semidefinite matrix. We prove that the same inequalities hold whenever $A$ is an $n \times n$ totally nonnegative matrix.
items.author: Mark A. Skandera

items.title: Beating the break-even point with autonomous quantum error correction
items.author: Yi Li, Q.-X. Mei, Quanlin Jie, Weizhou Cai et al.

items.title: Floquet-ADAPT-VQE: A Quantum Algorithm to Simulate Non-Equilibrium Physics in Periodically Driven Systems
items.summary: Periodically driven quantum systems exhibit many fascinating phenomena absent in equilibrium systems, but their simulation is more challenging than that of static systems. Consequently, quantum simulation of these systems offers greater opportunity for achieving quantum advantage. To build the foundation for simulating time-periodic Hamiltonians, we utilize the Floquet-Hilbert space formalism to transform the Hamiltonian into a time-independent form and provide its Pauli decomposition. Within this formalism, we develop a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm, Floquet-ADAPT-VQE, that produces three key quantities that govern periodically driven quantum dynamics: the quasienergy, the associated Floquet eigenstates, and expectation values of observables with respect to these eigenstates. The latter is achieved by applying a fixed-depth quantum circuit to an initial Floquet eigenstate—an efficient construction made possible by the Floquet-Hilbert space formalism. We also identify a suitable auxiliary initial state whose squared Floquet energy is independent of the number of auxiliary qubits as well as the driving frequency, which leads to better convergence with fewer ADAPT iterations. We demonstrate our algorithm by performing numerical simulations on a periodically driven XYZ model with a magnetic field. We also explore potential applications of our algorithm for studying various non-equilibrium phenomena in periodically driven systems.
items.author: Abhishek Kumar, Karunya Shirali, Nicholas J. Mayhall, Sophia E. Economou et al.

items.title: Noise-Induced Thermalization in Quantum Systems
items.summary: Abstract In the current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum era, noise is widely regarded as the primary obstacle to achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, certain stages of the quantum computing pipeline can, in fact, benefit from this noise. In this work, we exploit the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis to show that O(1) number of noise occurrences can accelerate a fundamental task in quantum computing -- the preparation of Gibbs states. We demonstrate this behavior using classical simulations with Haar-random and phase-flip noise, respectively, on a spin-1/2 chain with a local Hamiltonian. Our non-integrable model sees ~3.5x faster thermalization in the presence of noise, while our integrable model reaches a state that lies between a generalized Gibbs state and a Gibbs state due to noise. Since certifying a local Gibbs state is relatively easy on a quantum computer, our approach provides a new practical solution to a key problem in quantum computing. More broadly, these results establish a new paradigm in which noise can be harnessed on quantum computers, enabling practical advantages before the years of fault-tolerance.
items.author: Sameer Dambal, Yu Zhang, Eric Bittner, Pavan Hosur

items.title: Generating persistent-current superpositions in Bose-Einstein condensates using dynamic optical potentials
items.summary: Precise and flexible manipulation of the motional state of ultracold atoms is a fundamental enabling technology for diverse applications such as quantum sensing and quantum computation. In this paper we propose a general, simple and highly efficient method to engineer the motional state of a Bose-Einstein condensate with time-dependent optical fields, which can be realized experimentally with existing light sculpting techniques. We demonstrate numerically how to engineer superpositions of persistent currents in a toroidal trap, achieving very high fidelity. We also study in detail the stability of the state over time, and we present an analytical two-state model that approximates well the evolution of the state in presence of self-interactions.
items.author: Renzo Testa, Donatella Cassettari

items.title: Optimal Accelerated Life Testing Sampling Plan Design With Piecewise Linear Function Based Modeling of Lifetime Characteristics
items.summary: ABSTRACT Researchers have widely used accelerated life tests to determine an optimal inspection plan for lot acceptance. All such plans are proposed by assuming a known relationship between the lifetime characteristic(s) and the accelerating stress factor(s) under a parametric framework of the product lifetime distribution. As the true relationship is rarely known in practical scenarios, the assumption itself may produce biased estimates that may lead to an inefficient sampling plan. To this endeavor, an optimal accelerating life test plan is designed under a Type‐I censoring scheme with a generalized link structure similar to a spline regression, to capture the nonlinear relationship between the lifetime characteristics and the stress levels. Product lifetime is assumed to follow Weibull distribution with non‐identical scale and shape parameters linked with the stress factor through a piecewise linear function. The elements of the Fisher information matrix are computed in detail to formulate the acceptability criterion for the conforming lots. The decision variables of the sampling plan including sample size, stress factors, and others are determined using a constrained aggregated cost minimization approach and variance minimization approach. A simulated case study demonstrates that the nonlinear link‐based piecewise linear approximation model outperforms the linear link‐based model.
items.author: Sandip Barui, Shovan Chowdhury

items.title: Charge Transfer with a Spin. I: A Variational Constrained-CASSCF Framework for Investigating Charge Transfer in the Presence of Spin–Orbit Coupling
items.summary: Abstract Charge transfer in open-shell molecular systems can involve a delicate interplay between charge localization, orbital relaxation, and spin–orbit coupling (SOC), particularly near ground-excited state crossings. Here, we introduce a very inexpensive variational framework for treating these effects in odd-electron systems by extending the electron/hole-transfer Dynamically weighted State-Averaged Constrained CASSCF (eDSC/hDSC) method to include SOC. Our method incorporates the SOC Hamiltonian directly into the variational orbital optimization through complex-valued spinor orbitals, allowing orbital and spin degrees of freedom to relax self-consistently while preserving the time-reversal symmetry of doublet states. The method achieves smooth potential energy surfaces and rapid self-consistent field (SCF) convergence; moreover, from physically small to artificially large SOC strengths, the calculation can be converged to very tight thresholds across the whole potential energy surface. While the results presented here are for systems with two charge centers, as shown in the appendix, the theory is quite general and can be adapted to either a system of N charge centers or a metal-molecule surface with a continuum of states, so that charge transport (and not just charge transfer) can also be studied. The approach therefore provides a route toward ab initio studies of spin-dependent charge transfer and charge transport in molecular systems with nontrivial spin degrees of freedom.
items.source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
items.author: Alok Kumar, Zhen Tao, Joseph Eli Subotnik, Tian Qiu

items.title: Tracing the film structure of an organic semiconductor with photoemission orbital tomography
items.summary: Photoemission orbital tomography (POT) is a powerful tool for investigating the orbitals and electronic band structure of oriented layers of organic molecules. In many cases, POT allows conclusions to be drawn regarding the geometric structure, but so far it has been mainly applied to (sub)monolayers and rarely to bilayers, raising the question of whether POT can also provide structure information for thicker films. Here, we use POT to analyze the band dispersion in up to eight layers of $α$-sexithiophene (6T) adsorbed on Cu(110)-p($2\times1$)O. This linear oligomer turns out to be a textbook example that exemplifies the concepts of intra- and intermolecular band dispersion in molecules. Moreover, the rich band and orbital structure information available from POT for this system enables us to trace subtle changes in the crystal structure as a function of layer thickness. Specifically, we find that the periodicity of an intermolecular band changes with film thickness, revealing an increase of the intralayer distance between the molecules with the number of layers. At the same time, the momentum distribution of photoemission from the highest occupied molecular orbital of 6T discloses a decrease of the molecular tilt angle. Following the evolution of tilt angle and lattice constant with layer thickness, we observe -- purely based on electronic structure data -- that the surface-templated monolayer structure relaxes into the structure of bulk 6T crystals. The experimental findings agree well with the results of density functional theory calculations.
items.author: Monja Stettner, Siegfried Kaidisch, A. V. Matetskiy, Eric Fackelman et al.

items.title: Engineering quantum phases in two dimensions via vacancy-induced electronic reconstruction
items.summary: Topological phases of matter are commonly understood as emerging from crystalline symmetry and intrinsic spin-orbit coupling or, less frequently, from disorder-driven electronic renormalization. In realistic materials, however, structural defects naturally combine both ingredients. Here, we propose a universal mechanism by which atomic vacancies drive a topological phase transitions in two-dimensional semiconductors through electronic reconstruction. We show that vacancies generate locally ordered dangling-bond states governed by well-defined hopping and spin-orbit interactions, while their spatial distribution and mutual coupling introduce long-range disorder. As vacancy concentration increases, the hybridization of these defect states forms an emergent electronic subspace that undergoes a topological transition. By combining large-scale density functional theory calculations with an interpretable orbital based Hamiltonian, we find that this vacancy-induced electronic reconstruction can stabilize quantum spin Hall, quantum anomalous Hall, and Weyl semimetal phases. Our results indicate vacancies not as detrimental perturbations, but as active design elements capable of transforming trivial insulators into topological quantum matter, providing realistic routes for defect-engineered topological devices. Topological phases of matter typically arise from crystalline symmetry and spin–orbit coupling, but structural defects in materials can also play a crucial role. Here, the authors demonstrate that atomic vacancies in two-dimensional semiconductors can induce topological phase transitions, suggesting vacancies as transformative elements for designing defect-engineered topological devices.
items.author: Emmanuel V. C. Lopes, F. Crasto de Lima, Caio Lewenkopf, A. Fazzio

items.title: Physics-aware neural networks enable robust and full atomic structure determination via low-dose atomic electron tomography
items.summary: Atomic electron tomography (AET) determines the three-dimensional (3D) coordinates and chemical identities of individual atoms from a series of scanning transmission electron microscopy images taken at different tilt angles. However, under dose-limited conditions, particularly at electron doses lower than those typically used for standard AET of beam-robust inorganic nanoparticles, the reduced signal-to-noise ratio forces a trade-off among accuracy, robustness, and throughput. Here, we introduce a physics-aware, two-stage neural network (PANN) that incorporates physical constraints throughout its workflow to achieve accurate AET under low-dose imaging. First, a global-local 3D ResUNet refines the initial reconstruction and corrects geometric distortions in the volume. Second, the local density around each identified atom is encoded using 3D Zernike moments. These feature descriptors, along with the atomic coordinates, are then processed by a graph-attention Transformer to classify the elemental species. We benchmark the PANN workflow using a dataset of 42,588 simulated reconstructed volumes, covering diverse noise models, material morphologies, and dose settings. Under reduced-dose conditions relative to conventional AET of beam-robust inorganic nanoparticles, PANN significantly improves performance, reducing the atomic coordinate error and leading to an increase in the atomic recovery rate. The framework’s performance on retrospectively reduced-dose experimental AET data of metallic nanoparticles demonstrates robust post-processing capability within this material class. items.author: Yao Zhang, Lanyi Cao, Zhen Sun, Jihan Zhou

items.title: Sobolev Regularity of Compactified 3-Manifolds and the ADM Center of Mass
items.summary: Abstract In this paper we address the existence of preferred asymptotic coordinates on asymptotically Euclidean (AE) manifolds $$(M^3,g)$$ ( M 3 , g ) such that g admits an asymptotically Schwarzschildian first order expansion, based purely on a priori geometric conditions, which will then be used to establish geometric criteria guaranteeing the convergence of the ADM center of mass (COM). This problem is analysed relating it to the study of the regularity of conformal compactifications of such manifolds, which is itself explored via elliptic theory for operators with coefficients of very limited regularity. With these related problems in mind, we first establish Sobolev regularity properties of conformally compactified AE 3-manifolds via the decay of the Cotton tensor, improving on previous results. This allows us to construct preferred asymptotic coordinates on such AE manifolds where the metric has a first order Schwarzschildian expansion, which in turn allows us to address a version of a conjecture posed by C. Cederbaum and A. Sakovich concerning the convergence of the COM of such manifolds.
items.author: Rodrigo Ávalos

items.title: Model predictive quantum control: A modular approach for efficient and robust quantum optimal control
items.summary: Abstract Model predictive control (MPC) is one of the most successful modern control methods. It relies on repeatedly solving a finite-horizon optimal control problem and applying the beginning piece of the optimal input. In this paper, we develop a modular framework for improving efficiency and robustness of quantum optimal control (QOC) via MPC. We first provide a tutorial introduction to basic concepts of MPC from a QOC perspective. We then present multiple MPC schemes, ranging from simple approaches to more sophisticated schemes which admit stability guarantees. This yields a modular framework which can be used 1) to improve efficiency of open-loop QOC and 2) to improve robustness of closed-loop quantum control by incorporating feedback. We demonstrate these benefits with numerical results, where we benchmark the proposed methods against competing approaches.
items.author: Eya Guizani, Julian Berberich

items.title: Maximal Orbital Entanglement from Non-Interacting Fermions
items.summary: Orbital rotations are used in quantum many-body physics and chemistry to reduce the complexity of quantum states by compressing their correlation into a small set of relevant orbitals. In striking contrast, quantum information processing strives for the opposite: orbitals that maximize entanglement as a resource. Motivated by this, we prove that Slater determinants of $N$ fermions on a lattice of $d_A + d_B = d$ sites, although free of particle correlation, can carry up to $\min\{d_A, d_B, N, d-N\}$ ebits of orbital entanglement. Given enough particles and holes, this equals the maximum over all fermionic states. For arbitrary free states, we derive the maximal orbital total correlation in closed form for all bipartitions, the finest partition, and all partitions of up to five sites, using new majorization relations for Hermitian matrices. Taken together, these results turn mean-field states, the starting point of most many-body methods in physics and chemistry, into a viable resource for quantum information processing.
items.author: Damiano Aliverti-Piuri, Julia Liebert, Christian Schilling

items.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
items.summary: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.
items.author: François Gay-Balmaz, Tudor S. Ratiu, Cesare Tronci

items.title: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
items.summary: Quantum-centric supercomputing (QCSC) approaches, such as sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), combine quantum processors with high-performance computers (HPC), offering a promising route toward solving challenging electronic structure problems. However, implementation of QCSC approaches to large active space calculations is constrained by the associated number of qubits, deep quantum circuits, sampling cost, and large-scale Hamiltonian diagonalization. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a distributed QCSC framework that decomposes complex molecular problems into parallel sub-problems requiring fewer qubits, shallower circuits, and reduced shot budgets. A physically motivated, two-step aggregation scheme then reconstructs the global solution: first, a computational bit assignment strategy optimizes a cost function to appropriately map local bit indices to global ones, yielding a mapped tensor product state (MTPS); second, an inter-fragment correlation recovery module restores missing cross-fragment interactions. Herein, we employ a multi-layered generative machine learning architecture, starting with utilizing the recently proposed physics-informed generative SQD (PIGen-SQD) as a distributed QCSC solver, followed by a secondary generative module to model configuration distributions and identify dominant sectors of the global Hilbert space. For water and formamide dimers, our method achieves up to $95\%$ reduction in the diagonalization dimension while enhancing energy accuracy by an order of magnitude over conventional SQD. items.author: Chayan Patra, Prayas Ghosh, Adwait Patkhedkar, Rahul Maitra

items.title: Low-frustration block encodings by patch routing
items.summary: Block-encoding has emerged as a core primitive in many quantum algorithms, including quantum simulation. In this work, we design efficient and extensible methods for generating low-frustration block encodings of frustrated lattice Hamiltonians built from repeated local interaction patches through a technique we call "patch routing". We construct block encodings for a full Hamiltonian by first block-encoding a small local patch and then using a SWAP-style routing network to coherently apply the local patch encoding across the lattice. The expensive, local block-encoding cost is paid only once per query and is independent of lattice size, whereas the comparatively inexpensive routing network grows linearly with the lattice size, dominating at large sizes. Our method allows for a hierarchical structure in which larger patches can be block-encoded with small normalization factors, albeit at a higher (local, non-extensive) block-encoding cost, thereby reducing overall query complexity in an algorithm. We exploit symmetries and algebraic structures in local interactions to construct efficient block encodings, and we apply these techniques to the Heisenberg, Fermi-Hubbard, and honeycomb spin-liquid models. For a $120\times 120$ square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model near maximal frustration ($J_2/J_1=0.4-0.6$), our methods result in a $15-17\times$ reduction in the leading $T$ cost per qubitized-QPE run (ignoring initial state preparation and overlap) relative to prior state-of-the-art Pauli LCU constructions. Corresponding reductions are approximately $3\times$ for the $120\times120$ Fermi-Hubbard model at half-filling.
